concept_name: Friction Force — Static Grip Self-Adjusts Until It Breaks, Then Drops
source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.5 §5.9.1 (Laws of Motion — Friction) — table-of-contents scope only, teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: static friction is not a fixed value — it self-adjusts to exactly cancel an applied push up to a ceiling f_max = μₛN, past which the body breaks free and friction DROPS to the smaller constant kinetic value μₖN. Does NOT cover the incline decomposition or the tan θ = μₛ break-away angle (owned by shipped block_on_incline), the full friction-opposes-relative-motion direction subtlety, or stacked-block/belt/accelerating-frame contexts (V2, engine-out). Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine (docs/NEWTONS_LAWS_BODY_ENGINE_SPEC.md), pure configuration plus the pre-approved param_ramp one-shot knob, zero renderer edits. Does NOT touch the legacy friction_static_kinetic.json (old mechanics_2d, non-product).

real_world_anchor.primary: Pushing a heavy storage box across a floor. You lean into it — nothing. Push harder — still nothing, the floor answers you newton for newton. Then at one exact effort the box suddenly lurches free, and keeping it sliding feels easier than starting it ever did. That lurch is static friction losing to a smaller kinetic value the instant it lets go.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Anti-lock brakes on a car: a car stops best when the tyres do NOT skid, because rolling contact keeps the larger static grip while a skidding tyre only ever gets the smaller kinetic value.

m.name: mass of body A (and B in S4, the two-speed glide)

theta.name: incline angle — fixed at 0 throughout this concept (flat concept; block_on_incline owns the incline arc)

N.formula: normal reaction, N — m*g, constant at 49.0 N throughout this concept (theta = 0 fixed)

f.formula: friction magnitude, N — f_s = F while stuck (never exceeds mu_s*N); f_k = mu_k*N once sliding

a.formula: acceleration, m/s^2 — 0 while stuck; (F - mu_k*N)/m once sliding

F_net.formula: net force, N — 0 while stuck (the taught value in S1/S2/pre-break-S3); m*a once sliding

constraints: N = m*g at all times in this concept — theta = 0 is fixed and never authored as a control
f_s <= mu_s*N always while at rest; the reported static friction never exceeds its own ceiling
break-away occurs at F = mu_s*m*g exactly — this threshold is MASS-DEPENDENT on a flat push, the deliberate contrast with block_on_incline's mass-cancelling tan(theta_c) = mu_s
once sliding, f_k = mu_k*N < mu_s*N (mu_k < mu_s) and is CONSTANT for the rest of the slide, independent of both F and v — kinetic friction never varies with speed
STOP_EPS_V = 0.01 m/s: velocity below this is treated as exactly zero by the engine
T = 0 everywhere in this concept — no tension, no pulley, no hanging body (uncoupled Branch A bodies only)

aha_moment.statement: Friction matches your push exactly, up to one ceiling — then gives back LESS.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: As F ramps from 16 to 27 N, f tracks it exactly until 24.5 N, then the readout snaps down to 19.60 N and acceleration jumps from 0 to 0.98 m/s².

STATE_1.title: No Push — Zero Friction, Even Though the Ceiling Is Ready

scene_composition.text: No push, no friction — even though mu_s N = 24.5 N sits ready
f stays 0.00 while mg and N grow together as m is dragged
like leaning on a heavy storage box with nothing yet to push against

tts_sentences.text_en: Nothing is pushing this block, so friction has nothing to answer: f sits at zero.
Drag the mass up — weight and normal force N grow together, but friction stays 0.00.
Friction only exists when a push asks it to.

STATE_2.title: Static Friction Is an Answer — f Tracks F in Exact Lockstep

scene_composition.text: Push harder — friction rises to match, newton for newton
f tracks F exactly, every step of the ramp — never jumping to mu_s N
F_net stays 0.00 the whole time — friction is answering, not fixed

tts_sentences.text_en: Push harder and friction rises to match, newton for newton — watch the applied and friction arrows grow together while the block stays perfectly still.
The net-force readout holds at 0.00 the whole time.
So far friction always finds the answer... watch what happens when it can't.

misconception_watch.belief: Friction is always mu times N — a fixed value set by the surfaces.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The f readout equals the F readout digit-for-digit through the whole ramp — if friction were always mu_s N it would read 24.50 from the start, not climb from 16.00.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: mu_s N is friction's CEILING, not its value — below it, friction copies your push exactly.

STATE_3.title: The Ceiling and the Drop — Break-Away at F = 24.5 N

scene_composition.text: Push keeps climbing toward the ceiling
at F = 24.5 N the block lets go — f snaps 24.50 down to 19.60
a jumps 0 to 0.98 m/s^2 the instant it releases

tts_sentences.text_en: We reset the block and start the push from scratch.
Push keeps climbing; the block holds, holds, holds, until F hits 24.5 newtons, and it lets go.
Notice friction gave back LESS: the readout snaps from 24.50 down to 19.60.
That gap is why acceleration jumps from zero to nearly one metre per second squared.

misconception_watch.belief: All friction is the same — one fixed force.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The readout snaps 24.50 down to 19.60 at the instant of release: the grip that held the block was strictly larger than the friction that acts once it slides.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Static friction adjusts up to mu_s N; sliding friction is a smaller, fixed mu_k N — that is why the block lurches the instant it breaks free, and why it stays easier to keep moving than it was to start.

STATE_4.title: Kinetic Friction Ignores Speed — Fast or Slow, Same f

scene_composition.text: One block glides slow, one glides fast
both friction readouts read exactly 19.60 N — speed never enters
kinetic friction depends on N and the surfaces only

tts_sentences.text_en: One block glides slow, the other fast — yet both friction readouts read exactly 19.60 newtons.
Kinetic friction only cares about the surfaces and the normal force, never about speed.
Faster does not mean more grip lost.

misconception_watch.visual_counter: The v rows differ by 2.5 times, but the f rows are identical at 19.60 N.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Kinetic friction cares about N and the surfaces — not the speed.

scene_composition.text: change mass, push, mu_s, mu_k, starting speed — watch every arrow answer
f_s <= mu_s N   f_k = mu_k N

tts_sentences.text_en: Everything is yours now — change the mass, the push, both friction values, even the starting speed, and watch every arrow and reading respond.
